description:
05-09 (CPF4131 / TXMIGR TO(2)) end-to-end rehearsal, CONNECTION B of two (A=verify/part05-txmigr-to2, run first - B depends on the &LIB2 state A leaves behind: &LIB2/JUCHUM already CHGPF'd to the v2/JUDLV format, &LIB2/JUCHUL1 still in its ORIGINAL pre-JUDLV shape, and &LIB2/JU0900C, ZA0500, JU0300, RUNPROBE all compiled against the OLD JUCHUM/JUCHUL1 formats). See A's own manifest.json description for the full rationale behind the split (two-reviewer critique, 2026-09-27: the original single-connection design violated this harness's own hang-risk-last rule twice, and had an unresolved ODP-reuse risk between JU0900C/ZA0500's shared JUCHUD OPNQRYF and a later OPNQRYF in the same job).

Prerequisite check before running this connection: read connection A's own VFYLOG (work/verify/results/part05-txmigr-to2-*.json) and confirm RUNCHGPF finished without a 'RUNCHGPF: CHGPF failed.' message and PROBEB showed 'RUNPROBE: CPF4131 CONFIRMED' (if PROBEB did NOT show CPF4131, the premise this whole exercise rests on - that JU0900C/RUNPROBE's baked-in level ID actually disagrees with JUCHUM's current one - has not been established, and this connection's own PROBEA/RUNJU0300 results would not mean what this design assumes they mean). Also confirm no OTHER manifest targeting library2:"*B" (e.g. verify/part05-promote-rollback) has connected between A and B: TXMIGR's own Step 3 below recompiles EVERY *PGM object it finds in &LIB2, so a stray TK0100/TK0100D left there by that sibling manifest would show up as a harmless but confusing 'TXMIGR: could not recompile TK0100 (RPG).' line in VFYLOG (source member not found in &LIB2/QRPGSRC) - see A's own description for why this is expected to be harmless, not corrupting.

WHAT THIS CONNECTION DOES, IN ORDER: (1) recompiles TXSTATUS into &LIB (self-containment, same reasoning part05-ju0900c-baseline already uses for ZA0500/JU0900C, so this connection does not depend on &LIB still holding a working TXSTATUS from A or an earlier session), (2) re-adds &LIB2 to the library list (ADDLIB2 - a FRESH job needs this again; the previous connection's ADDLIBLE does not persist across connections, only across 'cl' steps within ONE wrapper job), (3) compiles and calls TXMIGR TO(2) LIB(&LIB2) - the tool this whole exercise is nominally about - via its own already-existing *CMD wrapper, through a tiny QCMDEXC helper (src/runtxmigr.clp, byte-for-byte identical to connection A's own runsetup.clp-style helpers, duplicated into this directory's own src/ for self-containment), (4) captures JUCHUL1's post-TXMIGR structure (SNAP2JL) and re-runs RUNPROBE (PROBEA) to see whether TXMIGR's own blanket 'recompile every *PGM' pass (Step 3) actually reached RUNPROBE/JU0900C and cleared CPF4131 for programs that read JUCHUM directly, (5) performs 05-09's own manual correct-order fix (lesson steps 5-6: DLTF+CRTLF of JUCHUL1, then CRTRPGPGM of JU0300) REGARDLESS of what TXMIGR's own Step 2 achieved on its own - this is the part of the lesson TXMIGR's own header comment already predicts it cannot do correctly (CRTLF with no preceding DLTF, and CRTPF/CRTLF confirmed to have no REPLACE parameter, so CRTLF alone very likely fails harmlessly with 'object already exists' against an ALREADY-EXISTING JUCHUL1 - exactly this connection's own starting state), (6) re-snapshots JUCHUL1 after that manual fix (SNAP3JL) to confirm it actually worked, (7) performs the lesson's own step 9 (CHGDTAARA of TXSTATE to 2 - TXMIGR's own SNDPGMMSG already says it never does this itself, 'update TXSTATE by hand if this tool did not', and its own source has no CHGDTAARA call anywhere) and re-reads TXSTATUS, and (8) as the LITERAL LAST step, CALLs JU0300 for the first time ever on real hardware in this repo.

CPJU0300F now runs DLTPGM PGM(&LIB2/JU0300) (MONMSG CPF0000) BEFORE the CRTRPGPGM REPLACE(*YES) (advisor review, 2026-09-27, matching verify/part05-13-tickets' own already-established DLTPGM-first idiom for the identical reason that manifest's own description gives): without this, a compile failure here would leave the STALE JU0300 (recompiled earlier, either by connection A's own CPJU03002 or by TXMIGR's own Step 3 above) silently in place - a stale, mismatched JU0300 quietly reproducing a level-ID problem at RUNJU0300 would look identical to 'the manual fix did not work' if REPLACE(*YES) alone were trusted to signal success. With DLTPGM first, a failed recompile instead leaves JU0300 MISSING, so RUNJU0300 would fail with an object-not-found-class message instead of silently running stale code - an unambiguous signal. Also note (not itself load-bearing for this connection, but the same mechanism 05-09's own 'column' discusses): CRTRPGPGM's own default CVTOPT is *NONE, and this step's own recompile of JU0300 does not specify CVTOPT() at all - so even though JUCHUL1 (once correctly recreated) now carries JUDLV (an L-type/DATE field), JU0300 recompiled here would NOT see it as an accessible field at all under that default, matching 05-09's own column point about CVTOPT(*NONE) making DATE/TIME/TIMESTAMP fields on an externally-described file invisible to a program that does not ask for them - harmless for JU0300 specifically, since its own I-specs never reference JUDLV, but worth noting as the same general mechanism the lesson text already teaches.

Why JU0300 alone, and not also a second JU0900C call (RJU0900A in the original single-connection design), is this connection's terminal step (advisor review, 2026-09-27, resolving a tension between two of the critique's own findings): RJU0900A would have re-CALLed JU0900C->ZA0500 after TXMIGR, mirroring RJU0900B in connection A to compare CPF4131 presence/absence - but PROBEA (step 4 above, RPG-free) already does this comparison directly and unambiguously, and connection A's own RJU0900B already exercised the RPG0907/CPF4131-adjacent escalation path once without incident (part05-ju0900c-baseline confirmed RPG0907 alone is harmless/non-hanging beforehand). Re-running the SAME JU0900C->ZA0500 call a third time across this pair of connections would add hang-risk-last budget pressure (only one step per connection can truly be last) without a new question it answers that PROBEA does not already answer more cleanly (an RPG0907 confound-free CPF4131 signal). JU0300, by contrast, has never been executed on real hardware at all (compile-only per part05-legacy-probe) - it alone carries a genuinely first-time, fully open hang-risk question, so it alone is this connection's terminal step. Note honestly what RUNJU0300 does and does NOT prove: because this connection's own step 5 (CPJU0300F) always recompiles JU0300 fresh, immediately after JUCHUL1's own last change (whether that change came from TXMIGR's Step 2 or this connection's own manual DLTF/CRTLF), JU0300's baked-in level ID is by construction always matched to JUCHUL1's CURRENT one by the time RUNJU0300 runs - so RUNJU0300 cannot, even in principle, demonstrate a CPF4131 on the JUCHUL1/JU0300 link specifically (a recompile-then-immediately-call sequence can never expose a level mismatch that recompiling itself just resolved). RUNJU0300 instead answers 'does this never-before-executed program run to completion without hanging or erroring, once every dependency has actually been rebuilt in the correct PF->LF->RPG order' - the lesson's own end state (05-09 step 8), not a fresh CPF4131 sighting. Whether TXMIGR's OWN Step 2 (CRTLF, unaided) actually succeeded or failed as predicted is answered instead by comparing SNAP2JL (right after RUNTXMIGR, BEFORE the manual fix) against connection A's OWN two JUCHUL1 snapshots - FDJL0 (the true pre-CHGPF baseline) AND, more precisely, FDJL0B (JUCHUL1 immediately after RUNCHGPF but before TXMIGR ever ran - the correct 'nothing has touched JUCHUL1 yet' comparison point, since it isolates CHGPF's own possible side effects on JUCHUL1 from TXMIGR's) - and against SNAP3JL/FDJL2 (after this connection's own manual fix): if SNAP2JL's row already differs from FDJL0B, TXMIGR's own CRTLF actually succeeded (contradicting its own header comment's prediction); if SNAP2JL still matches FDJL0B, the predicted failure is confirmed, and SNAP3JL should then show a further difference appearing only after this connection's own manual DLTF/CRTLF. (If FDJL0B itself already differs from FDJL0 - i.e. CHGPF-ing JUCHUM alone already changed what JUCHUL1 reports, without JUCHUL1 ever being recreated - see connection A's own notes.md for how that changes this reading.)

TXMIGR's own compile-time risk (unchanged from the original design, moved here verbatim since it does not depend on &LIB2's CHGPF state at all): tools/qclsrc/txmigr.clp DCLFs QTEMP/TXMDBR and QTEMP/TXMPGM, which are normally only ever created at RUN time by TXMIGR's own later DSPDBR/DSPOBJD OUTPUT(*OUTFILE) steps - meaning CRTCLPGM PGM(TXMIGR) could plausibly fail outright in a fresh job whose QTEMP does not already contain files by those exact names. CPTXMIGRRW below is a deliberately UNPRIMED CRTCLPGM attempt, run before anything populates QTEMP, specifically to observe whether that failure actually happens on real hardware. PRIMEDBR/PRIMEOBJ then run a throwaway DSPDBR/DSPOBJD OUTPUT(*OUTFILE) against &LIB/QCLSRC (an object that certainly exists) purely to populate QTEMP/TXMDBR and QTEMP/TXMPGM with the correct record formats in this SAME job, and CPTXMIGR retries the compile so the rest of this connection has a working TXMIGR regardless of whether CPTXMIGRRW succeeded on its own. All 'cl' steps here compile into and run as ONE CL program in ONE job (verify/lib/clgen.mjs), so QTEMP persists correctly across these steps. TXSTATUS/TXMIGR are invoked via QCMDEXC through tiny helper CL programs for the same *CMD-created-at-runtime reason connection A's own runsetup.clp/runchgpf.clp already document.

DSPFD *RCDFMT column names are not confirmed against any primary source in this repo (same caveat as connection A) - every DSPFD-derived collect step below reads 'SELECT *' rather than named columns.

OBJECT_STATISTICS collect step - read together with connection A's own final collect of the same query (its baseline, taken before TXMIGR ever ran): JUCHUL1's OBJCREATED changing between the two is NOT, by itself, clean evidence of what TXMIGR's Step 2 did, since THIS connection's own step 5 (DLTF+CRTLF) also changes it, unconditionally, regardless of whether TXMIGR's own CRTLF succeeded first - so an OBJCREATED difference conflates 'TXMIGR recreated it' with 'this connection's own manual fix recreated it'. SNAP2JL (captured BEFORE the manual fix) is the one piece of evidence in this connection that isolates TXMIGR's own effect; the OBJECT_STATISTICS collect below is kept mainly for the same JU0300/JU0900C/ZA0500/RUNPROBE OBJCREATED cross-check advisor review already suggested for connection A (a program recompiled by TXMIGR's Step 3 should show an OBJCREATED close to this connection's own run time, not connection A's).

TXSTATE/DBVER handling (unchanged from the original design): STATUS2 (right after RUNTXMIGR, before this connection's own manual fixes) is expected to still read DBVER=1 - per 05-09's own lesson text and txmigr.clp's own SNDPGMMSG ('...update TXSTATE by hand if this tool did not.'), TXMIGR itself never calls CHGDTAARA - confirming this documented tool gap on real hardware. CHGDBVER (this connection's own manual CHGDTAARA, lesson step 9) and STATUS3 then confirm the lesson's own manual finishing step separately, after the manual DLTF/CRTLF/CRTRPGPGM fix, not before it (matching 05-09's own step ordering: the DBVER bump comes after the actual migration is complete, not before).

Objects are deliberately left in &LIB2 afterward (no TXRESET/cleanup step) - &LIB2 (<USER>B) is the SAVF/scratch role, not a learner-facing library, matching connection A's own reasoning.

REVISION 2 (2026-09-27, second advisor review): (1) CLNFDJB (DLTF FILE(&LIB2/FDJL1) then DLTF FILE(&LIB2/FDJL2), both MONMSG CPF0000, right before SNAP2JL) added for the same reason connection A's own CLNFDJA/CLNFDJB were added - so this connection does not depend on DSPFD OUTPUT(*OUTFILE)'s own OUTMBR *ADD-vs-*REPLACE default, which this session's own WebFetch of ibm.com/docs/api/v1/content/ssw_ibm_i_75/cl/dspfd.htm (2026-09-27) could not pin down with full certainty (that same fetch DID confirm TYPE(*RCDFMT)/OUTPUT(*OUTFILE) themselves are valid syntax resolving to the real OUTFILE=QAFDRFMT/FORMAT=QWHFDFMT model - see connection A's own description for the full citation). (2) IMPORTANT READING GATE: confirm a line STARTING WITH 'TXMIGR: done.' actually appears in this connection's own VFYLOG before trusting SNAP2JL/PROBEA/SNAP3JL at all. Do NOT search for the literal text 'DBVER=2.' - txmigr.clp's own TXDONE label builds that part of the message via CHGVAR VAR(&DBVERC) VALUE(&TO) (a *DEC(3 0)-to-*CHAR(10) conversion) then %TRIM(&DBVERC): per this repo's own already-observed precedent (verify/part05-13-tickets/expected/notes.md's TXCHECK finding - a *DEC-to-*CHAR CHGVAR zero-pads, and %TRIM only strips surrounding blanks, not leading zeros), the real line will read 'TXMIGR: done. DBVER=0000000002. Run TXSTATUS to check; update TXSTATE by hand if this tool did not.' - a reader who greps for the unpadded 'DBVER=2.' form (matching 05-09's own lesson text, which quotes the unpadded form - the same already-known, not-yet-fixed TXCHECK-style discrepancy between lesson prose and actual zero-padded output) would wrongly conclude a successful run had failed. TXMIGR's own FAILSAFE label (tools/qclsrc/txmigr.clp) sends a MSGTYPE(*COMP) message and RETURNs normally (not an *ESCAPE), so RUNTXMIGR's own step-level MONMSG would never show 'FAILED' even if TXMIGR stopped partway through its own Step 1/2/3 (e.g. if $HOME/ibmi-kyozai/db/v2/juchum.pf, placed by connection A's own CVTJUCHUM2 step, were somehow missing by the time this connection's TXMIGR tries its own internal CPYFRMSTMF of that same path - TXMIGR's own Step 1 has no step-local MONMSG around that CPYFRMSTMF/CHGPF pair, only the program-level MONMSG(CPF0000, GOTO FAILSAFE)) - a silent partial failure would otherwise look identical to 'TXMIGR's Step 2 failed exactly as predicted' plus 'TXMIGR's Step 3 somehow missed RUNPROBE', which is a plausible-sounding but WRONG reading. Also confirm 'TXSETUP: done. DBVER=1.' appeared in connection A's own VFYLOG for the same reason (see that connection's own description). (4) A SEPARATE bug was found and fixed in tools/qclsrc/txmigr.clp itself this same session (see that file's own updated header comment for the full citation): the file's earlier OPNID(TXMDBR)/OPNID(TXMPGM) fix (added to its two DCLF statements to satisfy the 'RCVF needs OPNID when >1 file is DCLF'd' rule) had NOT also renamed the field references used everywhere below (&WHRELI/&WHREFI/&ODOBNM/&ODOBAT). WebFetch of ibm.com/docs/api/v1/content/ssw_ibm_i_75/cl/dclf.htm confirmed OPNID(value) RENAMES every DCLF-generated field variable to &value_fieldname - so once OPNID(TXMDBR)/OPNID(TXMPGM) took effect, those old unqualified names became simply undeclared, which alone would have failed CPTXMIGRRW/CPTXMIGR (this connection's own compile steps) outright on undeclared-variable errors, before RUNTXMIGR ever ran. Fixed by renaming every reference to match, and by switching to single-letter OPNID(D)/OPNID(P) rather than OPNID(TXMDBR)/OPNID(TXMPGM) (unrelated to the FILE(QTEMP/TXMDBR)/FILE(QTEMP/TXMPGM) qualifiers, which are untouched) - giving &D_WHRELI/&D_WHREFI/&P_ODOBNM/&P_ODOBAT (8 characters after &). Separately, whether a LONGER OPNID-generated name (like the original &TXMDBR_WHRELI) would even have been legal on CL variable-name-length grounds is NOT settled either way by anything this session found - a WebSearch-cited general rule suggests an 11-character-including-& cap, but dclf.htm's own example ('&FILE1_CUSTNAME', 14 characters after &) argues against a flat reading of that cap applying here, so this description does not claim to know which reading is correct; the short D/P prefix was kept anyway since it is legal under either reading. This was caught by static review before any real connection, exactly the kind of 'new/edited CL syntax must be confirmed against a primary source before this connection spends its one-per-15-minutes budget on it' check this session's own instructions call for - had the undeclared-variable problem not been caught, this connection's CPTXMIGRRW/CPTXMIGR steps would both have failed to compile, and every reading below (SNAP2JL, PROBEA, the whole TXMIGR Step 2 question this connection exists to answer) would have been moot.

(5) Two DIFFERENT rerun safety gaps remain, NOT fixed in this revision (noted here rather than silently left, per this repo's own honesty-about-gaps convention). First (a connection-A problem, not a connection-B one - see connection A's own manifest.json/notes.md for the same note there): TXSETUP's own CHKOBJ-then-skip-if-exists logic means connection A's own PRECLEAN (DLTF of JUCHUM/JUCHUL1) does NOT also reset &LIB2/TXSTATE back to DBVER=1 - so if connection A is ever RERUN against a &LIB2 that already went through a full A+B cycle, its own STATUS0 would already read DBVER=2 (left there by THIS connection's own CHGDBVER), contradicting connection A's own notes.md expectation ('DBVER=0000000001'). Fixing this would need a CHGDTAARA-to-1 step added to connection A's own RUNSETUP-adjacent steps, which neither this revision nor connection A's own Revision 3 added. Second, and specific to THIS connection (B): B itself cannot be meaningfully rerun on its own at all, even leaving the DBVER question aside - a second B run would start from JUCHUL1/JU0300 already fixed by the FIRST B run (this connection's own CHGDBVER/CRTJUL1/CPJU0300F), so SNAP2JL would already match FDJL2 rather than FDJL0B and PROBEA would already read clean - every prediction in THIS connection's own notes.md would be refuted by a state this connection itself created, not by anything genuinely new. B must always be preceded by a fresh run of connection A (see this description's own 'Prerequisite check' at the top) - a future session should treat 'B was rerun without a fresh A run' as the first thing to rule out if any of this connection's own predictions come back refuted.

(3) CPJU0300F's own recompile (and, for that matter, TXMIGR's own Step 3 recompiles of JU0900C/RUNPROBE, both of which read JUCHUM directly and both of which are being recompiled here for the FIRST time against a JUCHUM that now carries an L-type/DATE field, JUDLV) carries a residual, NOT fully ruled-out compile risk this design had understated: za0500.rpg's own header comment records a REAL, hardware-confirmed compile-time message (QRG4008, severity 10, halting the compile at this shop's own GENLVL) for an unrelated but structurally similar 'the compiler is unhappy about how a field is being read/ignored' situation (missing record-identification entries). Whether CVTOPT(*NONE)'s own handling of an ignored DATE-type field on an externally-described file compiles cleanly at severity 00, or instead raises some diagnostic-level message that could - depending on this shop's own GENLVL, unconfirmed - halt the compile, is NOT independently confirmed by any primary source this repo holds. If CPJU0300F (or, earlier, TXMIGR's own Step 3 recompiles of JU0900C/RUNPROBE) fails unexpectedly, this specific interaction (CVTOPT(*NONE) default plus a newly-added DATE field) should be the FIRST thing suspected, ahead of the UDS/runtime-array/LR-column items expected/notes.md already lists.

steps.label: CLNFDJB
steps.cmd:
DLTF FILE(&LIB2/FDJL1)
MONMSG MSGID(CPF0000)
DLTF FILE(&LIB2/FDJL2)
MONMSG MSGID(CPF0000)

steps.label: CPJU0300F
steps.cmd:
DLTPGM PGM(&LIB2/JU0300)
MONMSG MSGID(CPF0000)
CRTRPGPGM PGM(&LIB2/JU0300) SRCFILE(&LIB2/QRPGSRC) SRCMBR(JU0300) REPLACE(*YES)

steps.sql: SELECT OBJNAME, OBJTYPE, OBJCREATED FROM TABLE(QSYS2.OBJECT_STATISTICS('&LIB2', '*ALL')) X WHERE OBJNAME IN ('JUCHUM', 'JUCHUL1', 'JU0300', 'JU0900C', 'ZA0500', 'RUNPROBE') ORDER BY OBJNAME
